Its architecture, its grid of cobblestone streets, and its way of welcoming visitors possess something that has resisted time with a stubbornness that today feels like an act of identity. The neighborhood of San Telmo is the oldest in Buenos Aires. It was the first stable settlement of the colonial city and the seat of the 19th-century Buenos Aires aristocracy until the yellow fever epidemic of 1871 pushed them north. What remained—the mansions, the churches, the internal courtyards—transformed over time into conventillos (tenement houses) and, much later, into the densest cultural space in the city. This is the guide to understanding what San Telmo has that no other neighborhood in Buenos Aires can match, and how to explore it without missing what truly matters.
